## Data Analysis and Investigations on Mortality Rates in Scotland due to Coronary Heart Disease

---
class: inverse, center, middle

# Problem Statement 1: 
What is the trend in mortality rates of each gender due to coronary heart disease for those over 75 years old from 2015-2023?
---
#Reasons for investigating this problem
- to see the development in Scottish mortality rates caused by coronary heart disease throughout the years
- to investigate which gender and age group are more susceptible to death due to coronary heart disease
- to investigate any changes in mortality rates, and whether there is a change from external factors (eg. improvements in healthcare services, changes in lifestyles)


---
#Tidying Data
--
```{r}
#Selecting necessary columns from the dataset
hd_mortality <- hd_mortalitybyca [, c("Year", "AgeGroup", "Sex", "Diagnosis", "NumberOfDeaths", "CrudeRate", "Ca")]

```
--
```{r}
#Filtering and tidying the specific data
hd_mortality_year <- hd_mortality %>% 
  filter(
  Year != "2024p", 
  Ca == "S92000003",
  Diagnosis == "Coronary Heart Disease",
  AgeGroup %in% c("75plus years"),
  Sex != "All") %>%
    mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year)) %>%
  arrange(Sex)
```

---
```{r}
#Showing the results
hd_mortality_year
```
---

# Code
```{r}
#Creating a linear regression
mortality_female_fit <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(CrudeRate ~ Year, 
      data = hd_mortality_year %>% filter(Sex == "Female")) 

mortality_male_fit <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(CrudeRate ~ Year, 
      data = hd_mortality_year %>% filter(Sex == "Male")) 
```
---
```{r}
mortality_male_fit
```
--
```{r}
mortality_female_fit
```
---
```{r}
mortality_female_aug <- augment(mortality_female_fit$fit) %>%
                                mutate(Sex = "Female")

mortality_male_aug <- augment(mortality_male_fit$fit) %>%
                                mutate(Sex = "Male")

mortality_year_fit_aug <- bind_rows(
  mortality_female_aug,
  mortality_male_aug
) %>%
  mutate(residual = ifelse(.resid >0, TRUE, FALSE))
```

---
class: smaller-title
# Plots
```{r plot-iris, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(data = mortality_year_fit_aug) + 
 geom_point(aes(x = Year, y = CrudeRate, color = residual)) +
  geom_line(aes(x = Year, y = .fitted), linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = Year,y = .fitted), color = "purple")+
  geom_segment(mapping = aes(x = Year, y = CrudeRate,
                             xend = Year, yend = .fitted), color = "purple", alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Coronary Heart Disease Mortality Rates in Scotland (2015-2023)",
    subtitle = "For ages 75 years and above",
    x = "Year (2015-2023)",
    y = "Crude Rate (per 100,000 population)",
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Sex, scales = "free_y", axes = "all") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("hotpink", "forestgreen")) 
```
---
#Observations
.pull-left[
## General
- Overall, a downward trend in CHD mortality rates among people aged 75+ years old in Scotland, due to the negative sloping graphs
- CHD decreased by 26.4 deaths per 100,000 people annually
]

.pull-right[
##Male
- decrease of 19.6 per 100,000 people annually 
- 76.5% of variation in mortality rates is explained by YEAR
##Female
- 85.2% of variation in mortality rates is explained by YEAR
]
---
class: smaller-title

#Creating a residual plot 
```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(mortality_year_fit_aug, aes(x = .fitted, y = .resid, colour = Sex)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgray") +
  labs(
    x = "Predicted Mortality Rate",
    y = "Residuals",
    title = "Residuals vs Predicted (2015-2023)",
    subtitle = " For ages 75 years and above"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Sex, scales = "free", axes = "all") +
  theme_minimal()
```
---
#Observations
Female Residual Plot 
- 

Male Residual Plots 
- 

---
#General Limitations of the Model 
.pull-left[
Small Sample Size 
- 9 observed annual points
- not likely to establish an evaluation

Accuracy due to limited time period 
- high risk of extrapolation 
- models are good to highlight historical trends, but has uncertainty due to a low sample size 
]


.pull-right[
Relationship between the years 
- relationship between the years before is unknown (i.e. whether the year's result is due to previous years')

Unstandardized rates
- there is no information on the distribution of the ages withing the age bracket 
- i.e. 1 75 year old and 100 90 year olds (very skewed)
]
---
